# Avatar test fixtures

Everything here is generated from inputs this repo owns — text authored for the
purpose, spoken by [piper](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl) (MIT) using
voices whose training corpora are openly licensed: `en_US-ljspeech-high`
(LJSpeech, public domain) as `reference/a` and `en_US-libritts_r-medium`
(LibriTTS-R, CC BY 4.0) as `reference/b`. Nothing is copied from a private
corpus, so anything in here can be regenerated by anyone who clones the repo.

## The PCM clips

Three clips in voice `reference/a`, lang `en`:

| file | text | ms |
|---|---|---|
| `take-your-time.pcm` | "Take your time." | 937 |
| `that-is-good-to-hear.pcm` | "That is good to hear." | 1266 |
| `thank-you-for-your-time-today.pcm` | "Thank you for your time today." | 1639 |

Raw **s16le mono 24000 Hz**, the encoding the accurate leg is fed. Byte length
is the duration: `bytes / 2 / 24000`. Leading and trailing silence is trimmed,
so they are pure speech and carry **none** of the 250 ms inter-sentence pad the
streaming wire appends; tests that exercise the pad synthesise it.

Real synthesised speech and not a synthetic tone on purpose. The accurate leg is
pocketsphinx doing acoustic recognition; a sine wave or white noise tells you the
plumbing works and nothing about whether the recognizer produced mouth shapes
that belong to the words. Three clips spanning 0.9-1.7 s cover the range where
the fast leg goes from clearly better than recognition to roughly level with it.

## `duration_holdout.json`

The clips held out from the fit that produced
`src/voqalize_avatar/duration_table.json` — every 5th entry in manifest order,
by the same deterministic stride in `scripts/fit_durations.py`, so the accuracy
the tests measure is genuinely out-of-sample. Text and `audio_ms` only; no
audio.

The corpus behind it is 600 utterances per voice in the assistant's register,
stratified across character length from one-word acknowledgements to
two-sentence replies — because the model is `ms = ms_per_char * chars +
onset_ms` and a corpus bunched at one length fits a rate that only holds there.
